name: Giuliomax Menu Builder
author: giuliomax

sections.description:
Giuliomax Menu Builder lets you create fully customized navigation menus and embed them anywhere using the [menux] shortcode. Build your menu visually from the WordPress admin, style it with 20 preset themes or full manual controls, and it works perfectly on desktop, tablet and mobile.

v2.8 features a completely redesigned admin interface — accordion item editor, visual gradient picker, high-fidelity live preview with logo, guided onboarding tutorial — on top of an already complete feature set that includes a full Mega Menu system with 12 preset templates, a built-in search bar, WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, multilingual support and 4 mobile opening modes, all for free.

✨ Main Features

  • Accordion menu builder — every item collapses to a compact header showing the drag handle, title, role/device badges and a delete button; click to expand into clearly labelled sections (Label, Icon & Badge, Visibility & Behavior, Schedule & Conditions, Submenu); newly added items open automatically so you can edit right away; the whole panel is cleaner, faster to scan and easier to manage even with many items
  • Page + custom link support — use existing WP pages or external URLs, with target controls and role visibility
  • Advanced item targeting — show/hide items by user role, login state, device, current page, schedule, time range or UTM source
  • Menu location assignment — tag items for Primary, Footer, Sidebar or Mobile and render with [menux location="..."]
  • 20 preset themes — professionally designed themes with one-click apply and live preview: Ghost, Void Dark, Indigo Pulse, Aurora Night, Navy Command, Tropical Bloom, Evergreen, Cyber Matrix, Rose Silk, Sky Fresh, Newspaper Ink, Dev Dark, Ocean Electric, Violet Cloud, Swiss Pro, Cosmic Dusk, Warm Honey, Cloud Glass, Carbon Pro, Aegean Teal
  • Responsive mobile menu — automatic fit-based breakpoint or manual pixel threshold
  • 4 mobile opening modes — Dropdown, Fullscreen overlay, Drawer left, Drawer right
  • Hamburger style controls — Classic, Modern or Minimal icon appearance, alignment and colors
  • Link shape — configurable border-radius for pill-style or sharp links
  • Sticky header — fixed menu on scroll; “Match main menu” option (on by default) makes the sticky bar identical to the main menu with no extra configuration; custom background, shadow, padding and alignment available when the mirror is disabled
  • Scroll progress bar — page reading indicator that works on sticky or normal menus
  • Dark mode support — Light, Dark or Auto (follows OS preference)
  • Typography & layout — searchable Google Fonts dropdown (70+ fonts, lazy typeface preview), fallback font, size, weight, letter spacing, text transform and items alignment
  • Visual gradient picker — mouse-driven widget for the container background: live preview strip, Linear / Radial toggle, 8-direction compass rose, 0–360° angle slider and two colour pickers; syncs automatically when a preset theme is applied
  • Link animations — hover effects like Lift, Scale, Pulse, Bounce, Shake, Glow and Underline
  • Entrance animations — Fade, Slide, Zoom, Flip with duration, delay and stagger controls
  • Submenu styling — background, border, link color, shadow and animation controls
  • Logo support — add and position a logo image directly inside the menu bar; configure width, height, per-side margin and padding (Top / Right / Bottom / Left), vertical alignment and border-radius for circular or pill-shaped logos
  • WP Menu Integration — intercept classic theme wp_nav_menu() calls and replace them with MenuX output
  • Import / Export — save and restore menu configurations as JSON
  • Full reset — one-click button to delete all saved items, styles and settings
  • Multilingual ready — WPML, Polylang and TranslatePress support with language-specific item labels, each field labelled with a 2-letter locale badge (IT, EN, FR …)
  • High-fidelity live preview — real-time desktop/tablet/mobile preview that mirrors the actual frontend layout, padding, hover animations and gradient backgrounds so what you see in the admin matches what visitors see on the site
  • Search bar — optional magnifying-glass icon in the nav bar; opens a modal with two tabs: Menu tab searches all nav links by label, In page tab finds and highlights every occurrence of any text on the current page with full keyboard prev/next navigation
  • Onboarding tutorial — guided 4-step walkthrough driven by a 🐝 bee mascot that auto-starts on first admin visit and walks through adding items, picking a theme, previewing and exploring settings; can be replayed anytime from the admin toolbar
  • Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) — optional accessibility panel with keyboard navigation, focus ring, skip link, ARIA labels, touch targets, reduced motion and high-contrast support; disabled by default, enabled with a single master toggle

⚡ Mega Menu (free)

Build rich, full-width dropdown panels for any first-level navigation item — the kind of feature most plugins charge for.

  • Up to 4 columns per panel, each independently sized (% width or auto)
  • 5 column item types: clickable links, section headings, dividers, images, and arbitrary shortcodes / Gutenberg blocks
  • Icon + description on link items — give users context at a glance (e.g. “Dashboard — Analytics & reports”)
  • Icon on headings — visually group sections with a Font Awesome icon
  • Click-to-pick icon picker — browse and search Font Awesome 6 Free icons directly from the editor; no class names to remember
  • Drag & drop reordering of items within each column
  • Independent per-item toggle — enable Mega Menu on one or multiple nav items independently
  • Full-width panel that anchors to the navigation container, not to the individual link
  • Gradient backgrounds — 12 ready-made gradient presets (Dark, Purple, Indigo, Sky, Teal, Emerald, Sunset, Rose, Gold, Charcoal…) plus a custom gradient builder with direction, two color pickers and live apply
  • Panel appearance controls — padding, column gap, border radius, font size, link color, heading color, accent color
  • Smooth hover — 200 ms grace timer ensures the panel never disappears when moving the mouse from the trigger link to the panel content
  • Mobile-aware — collapses inline on small screens, or can be disabled on mobile entirely
  • 12 preset templates — one-click starting points covering the most common use cases; pick one and customize freely afterwards:
    • SaaS Product (4 cols, dark gradient — Features, Docs, Company, CTA)
    • E-Commerce (3 cols, white — Categories, Deals, Account)
    • Creative Agency (3 cols, purple gradient — Services, Portfolio, Studio)
    • News & Blog (3 cols, light — Topics, Sections, Connect)
    • Corporate (3 cols, sky gradient — Solutions, Industries, Company)
    • Restaurant (3 cols, warm gradient — Menu, Locations, Reserve)
    • Travel & Tourism (4 cols, ocean gradient — Destinations, Trip Types, Stays, Plan)
    • Online Learning (3 cols, dark indigo — Courses, Instructors, Community)
    • Healthcare (3 cols, white — Services, Doctors, Patients)
    • Real Estate (3 cols, dark charcoal — Buy, Rent, Services)
    • Fitness & Wellness (3 cols, red/orange — Train, Nutrition, Wellness)
    • Photography Studio (3 cols, dark — Services, Portfolio, Book)
  • Always-on live preview — the panel preview is permanently visible below the editor and updates in real time as you add, edit or reorder items — no toggle needed
  • First-time welcome screen — when a nav item has no mega menu yet, the editor opens a friendly welcome card with a “🎨 Choose a template” button that launches the 6 demo template picker, so users start from a solid base rather than a blank canvas
  • Per-link description color — each link item now has a color picker for its description text; supports full hex color with live preview swatch and a “Use default” reset checkbox

🎨 Style Options

  • Colors: background (solid or gradient with visual picker), links, hover state (solid or gradient), active state (solid or gradient), submenus, hamburger
  • Typography: Google Fonts (searchable, 70+ fonts with live typeface preview), font family, size, weight, letter spacing, text transform
  • Layout: gap, horizontal padding, vertical padding, container border-radius, items alignment, link border-radius
  • Mobile: breakpoint, opening mode, overlay color/opacity/blur, drawer width, open animation
  • Sticky: background, shadow, padding, alignment, transition, shrink effect, auto-hide on scroll
  • Mega Menu: background (solid or gradient), padding, gap, radius, font size, link color, heading color, accent color, mobile behavior

🔌 Usage

  1. Go to Giuliomax Menu Builder in the WordPress admin sidebar
  2. Build your menu items using the visual drag-and-drop builder
  3. Apply a preset theme or configure colors and style manually
  4. To add a Mega Menu: go to the Mega Menu tab, enable it on a nav item, click Edit Megamenu, add columns and items
  5. Place [menux] in any page, post, widget or template

🚀 Pro Version

The Pro version adds:

  • 📊 Click statistics — track which items users click, by device, role and date
  • 🎨 Custom CSS — write your own CSS rules directly from the admin panel
  • 📄 Multiple menus — create and manage independent menu configurations for different pages or locations

External Services

This plugin may connect to the following external service:

Google Fonts (optional)

If a Google Font name is entered in the Style panel (Typography tab), the plugin loads that font’s stylesheet from Google’s servers at https://fonts.googleapis.com. This request is made only when a Google Font is explicitly configured by the site administrator. The font name and the visitor’s IP address are sent to Google as part of the standard HTTP request.

  • Terms of service: https://developers.google.com/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Font Awesome icons are bundled locally within the plugin and do not load from any external server.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin from Plugins → Installed Plugins
  3. Go to MenuX in the admin menu
  4. Build your menu and copy the shortcode [menux]
  5. Paste [menux] wherever you want the menu to appear

Requirements

  • WordPress 5.8 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
sections.faq:
How do I display the menu?

Use the shortcode [menux] in any page, post, widget or block. For multiple locations on the same site use [menux location="footer"] etc. and assign items to that location in the builder.

Can I have different menus for different pages?

Not in the free version. Use role-based visibility or per-item device/page conditionals to adapt the menu per context. Full multiple-menu support is available in the Pro version.

Does it work with page builders?

Yes. You can insert [menux] as a shortcode block in Gutenberg, Elementor, Divi, WPBakery and most other builders.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. The menu HTML is generated server-side and compatible with WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache and similar plugins.

How do I add Font Awesome icons?

In the menu builder, each item has an icon field. Type the FA class name, e.g. fa-solid fa-house, or use the 🎨 Pick button to browse and search icons visually. Font Awesome 6 Free is loaded automatically.

Is it compatible with WPML / Polylang / TranslatePress?

Yes. This plugin automatically detects installed multilingual plugins and lets you set a label per language for each menu item.

Where is the mobile breakpoint?

Go to MenuX → Style → Mobile and set your preferred pixel breakpoint, or choose Auto to detect based on available space. Default is 768px.

How do I use the preset themes?

In the admin panel click Choose Theme (top bar). Browse the 20 preset themes, hover to preview and click Apply to try one live. Click Apply & Close to keep it, or Cancel to revert.

How does the Mega Menu work?

Go to the Mega Menu tab, enable the toggle next to a first-level nav item, then click Edit Columns. Add up to 4 columns, fill them with headings, links (with icon and description), dividers, images or shortcodes, then click Save columns. Not sure where to start? Hit ✨ Demo to load one of 6 ready-made templates.

Does the WP Menu Integration work with all themes?

It works with classic PHP themes that call wp_nav_menu() directly (e.g. GeneratePress, OceanWP, Neve, Kadence). Themes that use a custom header builder (e.g. Astra Header Builder) bypass wp_nav_menu() internally, so the integration cannot intercept them — use the shortcode approach instead.

Can I reset everything and start fresh?

Yes. Go to MenuX → Tools → Reset Everything and confirm. This permanently deletes all menu items, styles and integration settings.

Can I use custom CSS?

Custom CSS editing is available in the Pro version. In the free version you can target the .menux-container wrapper and its child elements from your theme’s stylesheet.
sections.changelog:
2.8.0

  • Sticky mirror — new “Match main menu” toggle (on by default) makes the sticky bar inherit all styles from the main menu automatically; custom background, shadow, padding and alignment options are hidden when the mirror is active and shown when disabled
  • Container border-radius — new field in Layout → Spacing to round the corners of the menu container
  • Page Load Animation — renamed from “Entrance Animation” with a subtitle clarifying it animates the menu on page load; duration/delay/stagger controls and the preview button are now hidden when “None” is selected and displayed inline on a single row when an animation is active
  • Entrance animation preview fix — the ▶ Preview button was targeting the wrong element (#menux-preview-wrap instead of #menux-preview-nav) so animations never played; fixed
  • Sticky menu fix — the sticky menu was immediately hidden after becoming fixed because the scroll-direction check fired in the same event frame; it is now always shown when it first becomes sticky and only auto-hides on subsequent scroll events
  • Logo in live preview — the admin live preview now shows the configured logo at the correct position (left/right/center); the logo updates immediately when selected, cleared or URL-changed in the Logo panel without requiring a save
  • Mega Menu preset modal — the template grid was clipped after the first row (6 of 12 visible); the grid wrapper now scrolls independently inside the modal so all 12 templates are reachable
  • Logo default left margin — changed from 0 to 16 px to match the existing right margin default; the logo no longer sticks to the left edge of the container out of the box

2.7.0

  • Help & Documentation modal — a full-screen contextual help overlay accessible from every section via the ❓ Help button in the admin toolbar; 12 sections covering every panel and field in the plugin, navigable via a sidebar without leaving the current admin page; content is rendered in English so the browser can offer translation into any language
  • Section persistence after save — saving settings now returns the admin to the same panel section the user was in rather than jumping to the top of the page; implemented via a hidden input that tracks the active section through the POST round-trip
  • Logo improvements — logo width default reduced to 40 px (was 120 px); margin and padding now use four independent numeric fields (Top / Right / Bottom / Left in px) instead of a raw CSS shorthand string; new border-radius field for circular or pill-shaped logos
  • Mega Menu — renamed to “Edit Megamenu” — the “Edit Columns” button, footer save button, dialog title and all references are now consistently labelled “Edit Megamenu” for clarity
  • Mega Menu — first-time welcome screen — when a nav item has no mega menu configured yet, the editor displays a welcome card with a “🎨 Choose a template” button that opens the existing 6-template demo picker, and a “start from scratch” fallback; replaces the previously empty blank state
  • Mega Menu — preview always visible — the live panel preview is now permanently shown below the editor and refreshes in real time on every change; the old “👁 Preview” toggle button has been removed
  • Mega Menu — per-link description color — link items in the mega menu editor now include a color picker for the description text, with a live hex label and a “Use default” checkbox to reset to the inherited grey
  • Mobile menu background removed — the “Dropdown background” toggle in the Mobile section was always-on, could not be disabled and did not save correctly due to a duplicate field name bug; the field has been removed; mobile menus now correctly inherit the container background set in the Colors section

2.6.5

  • Rock-solid search modal — the open/close click handler now runs unconditionally at page load, independent of any JS configuration flag; the modal element is looked up directly in the DOM at click time, so it opens correctly on every site regardless of caching plugins, shortcode order or data-injection timing
  • Full deferred-script support — the plugin JS now detects whether the DOM is already parsed when the script executes; if an optimisation plugin (WP Rocket, Autoptimize, etc.) adds defer, the init runs immediately rather than waiting for an event that has already fired — eliminating the silent “dead menu” symptom on optimised sites

2.6.2

  • Visual gradient picker for container background — a fully mouse-driven widget replaces the raw CSS text input: live preview strip, Linear / Radial type toggle, 8-direction compass rose for common angles, 0–360° fine-tune slider, two native colour pickers (Start / End) and a one-click Clear button; all changes update the live preview instantly; selecting a preset theme automatically syncs the picker controls to match the theme gradient

2.6.1

  • High-fidelity theme preview — the live preview now mirrors the real frontend layout: flex container with correct padding, link hover animations and transition duration are all rendered inside the preview frame so what you see while choosing a theme is what visitors will get; gradient container backgrounds are also shown correctly
  • Language locale badges — each multilingual label input now displays a pill badge with the 2-letter locale code (IT, EN, FR …) directly attached to the field, making it immediately clear which language is being edited without relying on placeholder text alone

2.6.0

  • Accordion menu builder — every item collapses to a compact single-line header showing the drag handle, title, role/device badges, chevron and delete button; click to expand into clearly labelled sections: Label, Icon & Badge, Visibility & Behavior, Schedule & Conditions, Submenu; newly added items open automatically so editing starts straight away
  • Streamlined Add pane — the two-card layout becomes a single card with Page and Link tabs; multilingual label inputs live inside the item detail section rather than a separate area, reducing visual noise
  • Polished drag-and-drop — items are flat rows inside one unified card separated by hairlines; the open item gets an indigo left accent and a light-tinted body; the drag handle highlights on row hover; the delete button appears only when needed; the dragging helper floats with a shadow for clear spatial feedback
  • Search modal viewport anchor — #menux-search-modal and the in-page search nav bar are moved to <body> at runtime, ensuring position:fixed always anchors to the viewport even when a CSS transform on the nav (entrance animation, sticky transition) would otherwise create a new containing block

2.5.0

  • Google Font picker — replaced the bare text input in Typography with a searchable dropdown showing 70+ Google Fonts grouped by category (Popular, Sans-serif, Serif, Display, Handwriting, Monospace); each font name is rendered in its own typeface, lazy-loaded via IntersectionObserver as you scroll; selecting a font instantly updates the live preview, including font-family, text-transform and letter-spacing; Quick Fonts block removed
  • Onboarding tutorial — floating 🐝 bee mascot auto-starts on first admin visit and guides the user through 4 steps: add menu items → pick a theme → live preview → explore settings; state stored in localStorage so it never repeats; replay any time via the “✨ Tutorial” button in the admin toolbar
  • Search bar — moved to the free tier; adds a magnifying-glass icon to the nav bar with a two-tab modal: Menu tab searches all nav links by label, In page tab finds and highlights all occurrences of any text on the current page with full keyboard prev/next navigation
  • In-page search fix — fixed a TreeWalker bug where only the first occurrence of a searched term was highlighted; the traversal now uses a two-phase approach (collect nodes first, then replace) to avoid invalidating the walker’s cursor during DOM mutation
  • Icon picker fix — raw Font Awesome class string no longer shown in the menu item input field (changed to type="hidden"); clicking “🎨 Pick icon” again after an icon was already assigned now works correctly
  • Consistent input styling — all text inputs, selects and icon buttons in the menu builder now use rounded borders (7 px radius) with a uniform indigo focus ring; previously some fields retained square browser-default borders
  • Mega menu hover fix — mega panel no longer closes when moving the mouse from inside the panel back to the trigger link; added a mouseenter listener on the trigger link to cancel the pending close timer

  • Close button color config — new color pickers in Style → Mobile → Overlay to set the icon color and background of the × close button shown in Fullscreen/Drawer modes; background set to none by default (user adds it themselves)
  • Hamburger button browser reset — fixed grey default background appearing on the hamburger when no background color was configured; the <button> element now gets background:transparent; border:none; appearance:none so only the 3 bars are visible unless a color is explicitly set
  • Preset themes: hamburger background removed — cleared hamburger_bg from all 6 preset themes that had a colored hamburger button (Indigo Pulse, Rose Silk, Sky Fresh, Warm Honey, Cloud Glass, Aegean Teal); users add a background themselves via settings if desired

2.4.0

  • Added complete Accessibility settings panel (WCAG 2.2 AA)
  • Keyboard navigation: full arrow-key menubar pattern (ARIA APG), Tab/roving-tabindex, Home/End, Esc to close submenus
  • Focus appearance: configurable ring style, color (with live 3:1 contrast validator), width and offset — covers new WCAG 2.4.11 and 2.4.12 criteria
  • Skip navigation link (WCAG 2.4.1 A) — rendered before the <nav>, visible on first Tab press
  • ARIA: aria-current="page" on active links, dynamic hamburger aria-label (open/close), aria-haspopup="dialog" on mega menu triggers, per-setting nav_aria_label

  • Motion: prefers-reduced-motion CSS media query, animation duration multiplier, configurable hover grace delay
  • Contrast: prefers-contrast: more CSS, forced-colors (Windows High Contrast) — system color tokens
  • Text spacing (WCAG 1.4.12): min-height instead of fixed height, overflow visible on link labels
  • Focus trap in mobile overlay (fullscreen/drawer) — Tab/Shift+Tab cycle within the panel, Esc closes
  • Focus-not-obscured scroll compensation for sticky header (WCAG 2.4.12)
  • ARIA live region for menu state announcements (WCAG 4.1.3)
  • Hamburger changed from <div> to <button type="button"> for native keyboard operability
  • Notification dots hidden with aria-hidden="true" + visually hidden SR text
  • Menux_Accessibility PHP class with generate_css(), output_skip_link(), output_live_region(), get_js_config(), save() and full option sanitization

  • Click-to-pick icon picker — browse and search Font Awesome 6 Free icons directly from the editor; no class names to remember
  • Drag & drop reordering of items within each column
  • Independent per-item toggle — enable Mega Menu on one or multiple nav items independently
  • Full-width panel that anchors to the navigation container, not to the individual link
  • Gradient backgrounds — 12 ready-made gradient presets (Dark, Purple, Indigo, Sky, Teal, Emerald, Sunset, Rose, Gold, Charcoal…) plus a custom gradient builder with direction, two color pickers and live apply
  • Panel appearance controls — padding, column gap, border radius, font size, link color, heading color, accent color
  • Smooth hover — 200 ms grace timer ensures the panel never disappears when moving the mouse from the trigger link to the panel content
  • Mobile-aware — collapses inline on small screens, or can be disabled on mobile entirely
  • 12 preset templates — one-click starting points covering the most common use cases; pick one and customize freely afterwards:
    • SaaS Product (4 cols, dark gradient — Features, Docs, Company, CTA)
    • E-Commerce (3 cols, white — Categories, Deals, Account)
    • Creative Agency (3 cols, purple gradient — Services, Portfolio, Studio)
    • News & Blog (3 cols, light — Topics, Sections, Connect)
    • Corporate (3 cols, sky gradient — Solutions, Industries, Company)
    • Restaurant (3 cols, warm gradient — Menu, Locations, Reserve)
    • Travel & Tourism (4 cols, ocean gradient — Destinations, Trip Types, Stays, Plan)
    • Online Learning (3 cols, dark indigo — Courses, Instructors, Community)
    • Healthcare (3 cols, white — Services, Doctors, Patients)
    • Real Estate (3 cols, dark charcoal — Buy, Rent, Services)
    • Fitness & Wellness (3 cols, red/orange — Train, Nutrition, Wellness)
    • Photography Studio (3 cols, dark — Services, Portfolio, Book)
  • Always-on live preview — the panel preview is permanently visible below the editor and updates in real time as you add, edit or reorder items — no toggle needed
  • First-time welcome screen — when a nav item has no mega menu yet, the editor opens a friendly welcome card with a “🎨 Choose a template” button that launches the 6 demo template picker, so users start from a solid base rather than a blank canvas
  • Per-link description color — each link item now has a color picker for its description text; supports full hex color with live preview swatch and a “Use default” reset checkbox

🎨 Style Options

  • Colors: background (solid or gradient with visual picker), links, hover state (solid or gradient), active state (solid or gradient), submenus, hamburger
  • Typography: Google Fonts (searchable, 70+ fonts with live typeface preview), font family, size, weight, letter spacing, text transform
  • Layout: gap, horizontal padding, vertical padding, container border-radius, items alignment, link border-radius
  • Mobile: breakpoint, opening mode, overlay color/opacity/blur, drawer width, open animation
  • Sticky: background, shadow, padding, alignment, transition, shrink effect, auto-hide on scroll
  • Mega Menu: background (solid or gradient), padding, gap, radius, font size, link color, heading color, accent color, mobile behavior

🔌 Usage

  1. Go to Giuliomax Menu Builder in the WordPress admin sidebar
  2. Build your menu items using the visual drag-and-drop builder
  3. Apply a preset theme or configure colors and style manually
  4. To add a Mega Menu: go to the Mega Menu tab, enable it on a nav item, click Edit Megamenu, add columns and items
  5. Place [menux] in any page, post, widget or template

🚀 Pro Version

The Pro version adds:

  • 📊 Click statistics — track which items users click, by device, role and date
  • 🎨 Custom CSS — write your own CSS rules directly from the admin panel
  • 📄 Multiple menus — create and manage independent menu configurations for different pages or locations

External Services

This plugin may connect to the following external service:

Google Fonts (optional)

If a Google Font name is entered in the Style panel (Typography tab), the plugin loads that font’s stylesheet from Google’s servers at https://fonts.googleapis.com. This request is made only when a Google Font is explicitly configured by the site administrator. The font name and the visitor’s IP address are sent to Google as part of the standard HTTP request.

  • Terms of service: https://developers.google.com/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Font Awesome icons are bundled locally within the plugin and do not load from any external server.
